input: Learn the basics of home electrical wiring safely

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Electrical wiring covers a huge range — from replacing an outlet to wiring a whole circuit. Knowing exactly which tasks or concepts to include shapes the entire learning path.
Whether this is for personal DIY repairs, helping a family member, or a professional stepping stone changes the depth and focus needed.
The type of home (older vs. new construction, rental vs. owned) and country/region affects which wiring standards, codes, and safety rules apply.
The amount of time available per week determines whether a structured course, a book, or short video tutorials is the most realistic format.
Some people learn best hands-on with practice kits, others through video or written guides — the right format dramatically affects retention and confidence.
What 'done' looks like matters: is it passing a test, confidently completing a specific job, or just feeling safe enough to attempt minor fixes?
Current experience level determines the starting point — a complete beginner needs safety fundamentals first, while someone with some DIY background can skip to intermediate topics.

gold.taskTitle: Learn home electrical wiring basics safely
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to build foundational knowledge and skills in home electrical wiring while prioritising safety.

questions.title: Which specific wiring tasks do you want to learn?
questions.description: For example: replacing outlets or switches, adding a new circuit, installing a breaker, running cables through walls, or all of the above. This defines the scope of the learning plan.

questions.title: Who are you learning this for — yourself or others?
questions.description: Is this for your own DIY home repairs, helping a family member, a landlord managing properties, or as a stepping stone toward a trade career? This shapes how deep and broad the learning needs to go.

questions.title: What country and type of home are you working in?
questions.description: Wiring standards differ significantly by country (e.g., NEC in the US, BS 7671 in the UK) and by home age or type. This determines which codes, voltages, and safety rules are relevant.

questions.title: How many hours per week can you dedicate to learning?
questions.description: Time availability determines whether a structured multi-week course, a weekend crash course, or bite-sized daily sessions is the most realistic and effective approach.

questions.title: Do you prefer hands-on practice, videos, or reading?
questions.description: Learning format preference — such as a physical practice board, YouTube tutorials, a textbook, or an online course — determines which resources to prioritise.

questions.title: What does success look like when you finish learning?
questions.description: For example: confidently completing a specific job, passing a homeowner permit inspection, feeling safe enough for minor fixes, or reaching a level where you could tackle any basic repair independently.

questions.title: What is your current experience level with electrical work?
questions.description: Complete beginner with no prior knowledge, some DIY experience, or familiar with basic concepts but lacking formal training — this sets the starting point for the entire plan.
